mainTopic: Why gentile cheese is forbidden: lessons from the משנה's dialogue, why the reason was kept hidden, and the reasons given by רבי יהושע בן לוי, רבי חנינא and שמואל
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's discussion of the משנה where רבי ישמעאל asks רבי יהושע why gentile cheese is forbidden. First the גמרא learns two rules from their talk. The stomach contents of animals forbidden for benefit are permitted, but the stomach contents of עבודה זרה animals are forbidden. It then asks why רבי יהושע did not answer that the forbidden part is not noticeable, as with מורייס. The answer is that rennet, which makes the cheese set, counts as if it is really there. Next the גמרא explains the פסוק 'כי טובים דודיך מיין' and why רבי יהושע used it as a hint to stop asking: the ban was a new גזירה, and its reason was kept quiet for a year. רבי יהושע בן לוי says the real reason was ניקור (snake venom), and רבי ירמיה attacks this. רבי חנינא and שמואל then give other reasons. The גמרא challenges שמואל from his own words about a נבילה's stomach, and it begins to resolve this at the end of the amud.

steps.title: Stomach contents of animals forbidden for benefit are permitted
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's discussion, the גמרא infers that animals forbidden for benefit (איסורי הנאה) still have permitted stomach contents (פרש).
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn from here that with animals forbidden for benefit, their stomach contents are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the earlier part of the משנה's conversation. Even when an animal itself is forbidden for benefit, what is inside its stomach is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's discussion treated the curdling stomach of forbidden animals as something that could be permitted. The גמרא turns this into a general rule. The stomach contents are not counted as part of the forbidden animal, so the איסור הנאה on the animal does not spread to them.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; 'we can learn from this that…'
Things you are not allowed to get any benefit from
Are permitted
Stomach contents or excrement of an animal

phrases.english: We learn by inference that animals forbidden for benefit
their stomach contents are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of the משנה's dialogue from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרש of animals forbidden for benefit is permitted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An איסור הנאה on an animal does not extend to its stomach contents.

steps.title: Stomach contents of idolatrous animals are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יהושע's reason (calves of עבודה זרה) and רבי ישמעאל's reply, the גמרא infers that the stomach contents of עבודה זרה animals are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at what happened in the משנה. רבי יהושע said the cheese is forbidden because gentiles curdle it with the stomach of calves used for עבודה זרה. רבי ישמעאל answered, 'If so, why didn't they forbid benefit from it too?' From this exchange we learn that the stomach contents of עבודה זרה animals are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a second lesson from the משנה. Animals of עבודה זרה are different: even their stomach contents are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל did not argue that the stomach of an idolatrous calf is permitted. He only asked why the cheese is not forbidden for benefit too. That shows both rabbis agreed the stomach of an עבודה זרה animal is truly forbidden. So עבודה זרה is stricter than other איסורי הנאה from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: They curdle (set) the cheese
Stomach, used to curdle milk into cheese
Calves used for idol worship
Answers him back
Is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Two rules come out of the משנה. The stomach contents of ordinary איסורי הנאה are permitted. The stomach contents of עבודה זרה animals are forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two inferences. Step 1 is about animals forbidden for benefit in general, which have permitted stomach contents. This step is only about עבודה זרה, which is stricter.

phrases.english: And from the fact that he said to him
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע speaking to רבי ישמעאל in the משנה.

phrases.english: because they curdle it
with the stomach of calves of idol worship,
and he answered him back:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן לָמָּה לֹא אֲסָרוּהָ בַּהֲנָאָה —
phrases.english: If so, why didn't they forbid it for benefit?
we learn by inference that with idol worship animals
their stomach contents are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּקֵיבַת עֶגְלֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second inference from the same משנה, giving a stricter rule for עבודה זרה that contrasts with step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרש of עבודה זרה animals is forbidden.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עבודה זרה is stricter than other איסורי הנאה: its prohibition reaches even the stomach contents.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יהושע say the forbidden part isn't noticeable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע did not answer רבי ישמעאל by saying the cheese is permitted for benefit because no actual forbidden substance is noticeable in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he should have answered him: benefit is allowed because the forbidden thing is not actually there in a noticeable way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבי יהושע handled the conversation. He changed the subject, yet he seemed to have an easy answer available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל asked why the cheese is not forbidden for benefit if it was curdled with an idolatrous calf's stomach. The גמרא suggests a simple answer. The forbidden stomach is not recognizable in the finished cheese (ליתיה לאיסורא בעיניה), so only eating is forbidden and benefit is allowed. So why did רבי יהושע avoid the question?

keyTerms.meaning: But let him answer back
The forbidden substance is not present in its own noticeable form

phrases.english: But let him answer him back,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking why רבי יהושע changed the subject instead of answering.

phrases.english: that it is because the forbidden substance is not there in a noticeable form!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַהְדַּר לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵיתֵיהּ לְאִיסּוּרָא בְּעֵינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the inferences back to the משנה's dialogue and questions why רבי יהושע avoided רבי ישמעאל's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's choice to change the subject instead of answering רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An easy answer was available: the forbidden ingredient is not noticeable in the cheese, so benefit should be allowed. Why didn't he say it?

steps.title: Proof from fish brine (מורייס)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its question with מורייס. The רבנן permit benefit from it, and the reason must be that the forbidden ingredient is not noticeable.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, take מורייס (fish brine). According to the רבנן, it is not forbidden for benefit. What is the reason? Isn't it because the forbidden substance is not there in a noticeable form?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its question from step 3. It points to a known case where this exact reasoning is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן allow benefit from מורייס, and the only reason that fits is ליתיה לאיסורא בעיניה. That shows the reasoning is real and accepted. So רבי יהושע could have used the same reason for the cheese, which makes the question in step 3 stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A fish brine or sauce made by gentiles
The Sages (the majority view)
What is the reason?
Is it not…? (introduces the obvious answer)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ליתיה לאיסורא בעיניה is an accepted reason to permit benefit. This sets up the challenge the גמרא will need to answer next.

phrases.english: For after all, fish brine,
according to the Sages, who did not forbid it for benefit,
what is the reason?
Is it not because the forbidden substance is not there in a noticeable form?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא מוּרְיָיס לְרַבָּנַן דְּלָא אַסְרוּהּ בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the question in step 3 with a parallel case.
steps.raayaObject: That ליתיה לאיסורא בעיניה is a valid reason to permit benefit, so רבי יהושע could have used it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן's ruling that מורייס is not forbidden for benefit

steps.title: Rennet that firms the cheese counts as a real forbidden item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the question from מורייס. Rennet is what curdles the cheese, so it is treated as if the forbidden item is really present.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Here, since the rennet is what makes the cheese stand firm, it is treated like something whose forbidden item is actually there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from steps 3-4. It explains why רבי יהושע could not say 'the forbidden part is not noticeable, so benefit is allowed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מורייס the forbidden ingredient just gets lost, so the רבנן allow benefit. In cheese the rennet does a job: it makes the milk firm. Because the whole cheese depends on it, the rennet counts as if it is fully there. So the proof from מורייס does not work for cheese.

keyTerms.meaning: It actually makes it stand, meaning it curdles and firms the cheese
The forbidden item is present in its actual form

steps.whatToRemember: Something forbidden that does a job in the food, like rennet firming cheese, is treated as if it is really there, even when you cannot see it.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say the rennet can be seen or tasted in the cheese. It cannot. The point is that its job makes it count as present.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the rule that an ingredient which sets or forms a food (דבר המעמיד) is not cancelled out, even in a small amount.

phrases.english: They say: here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the cheese, as opposed to the מורייס from the last step.

phrases.english: since it actually makes it stand firm,
phrases.notes: Literally 'makes it stand.' The rennet is what turns the milk into solid cheese.

phrases.english: it is considered like something that has
its forbidden item present in its actual form.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאוֹקֹמֵיה קָא מוֹקֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3, as strengthened by the מורייס case in step 4. Cheese is different because the rennet is what makes it set.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison of cheese to מורייס, and so rejects the question of why רבי יהושע did not give the 'not noticeable' answer
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In מורייס the forbidden part has no job. In cheese the rennet firms the food, so it counts as present.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the case at hand differs from the case the challenge relied on. An ingredient that sets the food (cheese) is not like one that is simply lost in it (מורייס).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cheese is like מורייס: the forbidden ingredient is not noticeable, so רבי יהושע could have permitted benefit for that reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rennet that curdles the cheese counts as a forbidden item that is really present, so the 'not noticeable' answer was not available to רבי יהושע.

steps.title: What does the verse 'For your love is better than wine' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, where רבי יהושע changed the subject, and asks what the פסוק he raised means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He turned him to another matter,' and so on. What is the meaning of 'For your love is better than wine'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, where רבי יהושע changed the subject to a פסוק in שיר השירים. It asks what that פסוק means, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new section about the end of the משנה. Before asking why רבי יהושע chose this פסוק, the גמרא first wants to understand the פסוק itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned his attention to another matter
And so on (the quote of the משנה continues)
Your love, or your beloved ones

phrases.english: He turned him to another matter, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, where רבי יהושע changed the subject instead of answering רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'For your love is better than wine'?
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 1:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on the end of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the פסוק 'כי טובים דודיך מיין'

steps.title: The words of the חכמים are sweeter than the wine of the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that כנסת ישראל tells הקב״ה that the words of His beloved ones, the חכמים, are sweeter than the תורה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: כנסת ישראל said before הקב״ה, 'Master of the world, the words of Your beloved ones are sweeter to me than the wine of the תורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question by explaining the פסוק. 'דודיך' means the חכמים, and 'wine' means the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as praise for the words of the חכמים, more than the written תורה. This fits the משנה's topic, because the ban on non-Jews' cheese is a rule of the חכמים, not a rule written in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The Jewish people as a whole
Sweet, pleasant
The words of Your beloved ones, the חכמים

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
The congregation of Israel said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
the words of Your beloved ones are sweeter to me
phrases.notes: He is reading 'דודיך' as 'Your beloved ones,' meaning the חכמים.

phrases.english: than the wine of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words of the חכמים are sweeter than the wine of the תורה

steps.title: Why did רבי יהושע pick this particular verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is special about this פסוק that רבי יהושע chose to ask about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about this verse, that he asked him about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע chose this פסוק out of all the פסוקים he could have asked about. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the subject could have been done with any question. The גמרא assumes רבי יהושע picked this פסוק on purpose and wants to find the hidden message.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
That he asked him

phrases.english: What is different about this verse, that he asked him about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the פסוק, asks why it was chosen
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהושע chose this פסוק

steps.title: The start of the verse hints: keep your lips closed
steps.stepSummary: The beginning of the פסוק, 'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth,' hints to רבי ישמעאל to press his lips together and not rush to reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said, and some say רבי שמעון בר אמי: He was hinting to him from the start of the verse, 'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.' He was telling him: 'ישמעאל my brother, press your lips together and do not rush to answer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that רבי יהושע wanted the first words of that פסוק. They hint, 'Close your lips and stop asking.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: When lips kiss, they press together. רבי יהושע used this image as a polite hint that רבי ישמעאל should stop pushing for the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: From the beginning of the verse
Press your lips together
Do not rush to answer

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said,
and some say Rabbi Shimon bar Ami:
He was telling him from the beginning of the verse,
'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 1:2, the same פסוק, just its first half.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yishmael, my brother,
press your lips one against the other
and do not rush to answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first half of the פסוק hints to רבי ישמעאל to close his lips and stop questioning

steps.title: Why did רבי ישמעאל have to stop asking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע did not want רבי ישמעאל to keep questioning him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע told רבי ישמעאל to stop asking questions. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a student or colleague is allowed to ask for the reason behind a rule. So the גמרא wants to know why this case was different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why should רבי ישמעאל stop asking?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reason behind the hint in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי ישמעאל was told not to question further

steps.title: It was a new decree, so people should not pick at it
steps.stepSummary: עולא, or רב שמואל בר אבא, says the ban on the cheese was a new גזירה, and a new גזירה should not be questioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, and some say רב שמואל בר אבא: It was a new decree, and we do not question it.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the cheese ban was a brand-new גזירה. People should not pick at a new גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason for a new rule spreads, people may decide the reason does not apply to them and start ignoring the rule. So רבי יהושע kept the reason quiet until the rule was well accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: A new decree of the חכמים
Pick at, question, cast doubt on

phrases.english: Ulla said,
and some say Rav Shmuel bar Abba:
It is a new decree,
and we do not question it.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה חֲדָשָׁה הִיא, וְאֵין מְפַקְפְּקִין בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban was a new גזירה, and a new גזירה is not questioned

steps.title: What was the real reason for the decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the actual reason for the cheese גזירה was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the decree?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know why the reason was kept quiet, the גמרא asks what the reason actually was. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasons suggested in the משנה were only answers that רבי יהושע used to push רבי ישמעאל away. The גמרא wants the real reason behind the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: What was the decree (its reason)?

phrases.english: What was the decree?
phrases.notes: He means: what was the reason behind the ban on the cheese?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 11 by asking for the real reason
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true reason for the ban on non-Jews' cheese

steps.title: The reason was the fear of snake venom (ניקור)
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the cheese was banned because of ניקור, the worry that a snake left venom in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: It is because of ניקור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first explanation of the real reason. The cheese was banned because of ניקור, a danger to health.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניקור means a snake may have bitten into the cheese and left venom. This reason is about danger, not about עבודה זרה or forbidden foods.

keyTerms.meaning: Puncturing: the fear that a snake bit into the food and left venom
Because of

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, the real reason for the ban on non-Jews' cheese is ניקור, a fear of snake venom.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Because of puncturing.
phrases.notes: The worry is that a snake bit into the cheese and left its venom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree was because of ניקור, the danger of snake venom

steps.title: Why not just tell him the reason?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason was ניקור, רבי יהושע should simply have told רבי ישמעאל so.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him just tell him: it is because of the snake-venom worry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. If the reason was ניקור, why did רבי יהושע change the subject instead of saying it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave a simple, clear reason for the ban. A simple reason should be easy to share, so hiding it looks strange. This sets up the next step, which explains why he kept quiet.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him say to him (why didn't he just say?)
Puncturing: the worry that a snake bit the cheese and left venom

phrases.english: But let him say to him: because of puncturing!
phrases.notes: "Him" means רבי יהושע speaking to רבי ישמעאל, in the story told in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason given in step 13 to question רבי יהושע's behavior in the story
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's choice to avoid answering רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason was simple and known, there was no need to dodge the question.

steps.title: New decrees were not explained for a year
steps.stepSummary: Following עולא, the reasons for new decrees in ארץ ישראל were hidden for twelve months so people would not belittle them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows עולא, who said: when they made a decree in ארץ ישראל, they did not reveal its reason for twelve months, in case someone disagreed with the reason and came to treat the decree lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע was following a known practice: the reason for a new גזירה was kept secret for its first year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was never that the reason was unknown. The worry was that if people heard the reason too early, some would think it weak and stop keeping the decree. After a year the decree is firmly accepted, and the reason can safely be shared.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree made by the חכמים
The West, meaning ארץ ישראל
They do not reveal the reason
To treat lightly, to belittle

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the חכמים thought about how a new decree would be received, and protected it until it was firmly in place.

phrases.english: In line with עולא, as עולא said:
When they decree a decree in the West,
phrases.notes: "The West" is how the בבלי refers to ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: they do not reveal the reason
until twelve months of the year,

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא אִיכָּא אִינִישׁ דְּלָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: perhaps there is a person who does not agree with it
and will come to treat it lightly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Policy explanation: there was a deliberate practice of keeping the reasons for new decrees hidden
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hiding the reason means there was no clear reason, or that רבי יהושע didn't want to share it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason existed, but new decrees were left unexplained for a year to protect them.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה attacks the snake-venom reason
steps.stepSummary: If ניקור were the reason, dry or aged cheese should be permitted, since venom stops food from drying and aging.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה mocked this reason: if so, dry cheese should be permitted and aged cheese should be permitted! For רבי חנינא said: something dry is permitted, because venom does not let it dry; something aged is permitted, because venom does not let it age.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's reason from step 13. He argues that the reason would not explain banning all cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא taught that venom stops food from drying out or aging properly. So cheese that dried or aged normally must not contain venom. If ניקור were the only worry, that kind of cheese should be allowed, but the ban covers all cheese.

keyTerms.meaning: Mocks, sharply challenges
But if so (introducing a strange result)
Dry
Aged, old
Should be permitted

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה mocked it:
But if so, dry cheese should be permitted,
aged cheese should be permitted!
For רבי חנינא said:
Dry is permitted, it does not let it dry;
phrases.notes: "It" is the snake's venom. Food with venom in it won't dry properly, so dry food must be safe.

phrases.english: aged is permitted, it does not let it age.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the reason given in step 13 and attacks it
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reason of ניקור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Venom stops drying and aging, so dry or aged cheese is clearly venom-free. The ניקור reason therefore can't explain a ban on all cheese.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: drops of milk remain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא gives a different reason: cheese always has tiny drops of milk left in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: because it is impossible for the cheese to be without little drops of milk.
steps.whatsHappening: Since ניקור was challenged, the גמרא brings a new reason for the ban from רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason does not depend on venom, so drying or aging the cheese doesn't help. The concern is the milk itself that stays inside the cheese.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiny drops of milk
It is impossible

phrases.english: רבי חנינא said:
Because it is impossible for it
to be without drops of milk,
phrases.notes: The worry is that some tiny drops of forbidden milk stay stuck inside the cheese.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ בְּלֹא צִחְצוּחֵי חָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reason after the ניקור reason was challenged
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cheese is forbidden because drops of milk always remain in it.

steps.title: שמואל: curdled in a נבילה's stomach skin
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the cheese is forbidden because it is curdled using the stomach skin of a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: because they curdle it with the skin of the stomach of a נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second new reason, from שמואל. He focuses on how the cheese is made to set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheese is made firm with something from an animal's stomach. שמואל says the gentiles use the stomach skin of a נבילה, an animal that was not properly slaughtered, so the cheese absorbs something forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They curdle it, make it set firm
The skin of the stomach
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
Because they curdle it
with the skin of the stomach of a נבילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּעוֹר קֵיבַת נְבֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second alternative reason, alongside רבי חנינא's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cheese is forbidden because it is curdled with the stomach skin of a נבילה.

steps.title: Does שמואל really permit the stomach contents?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's words imply that the stomach contents themselves are permitted, but a משנה says the stomach of a נבילה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that the stomach itself is permitted. But did שמואל really say that? Didn't we learn in a משנה: the stomach of a gentile's animal and of a נבילה is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from שמואל: only the skin is a problem, and what's inside the stomach is fine. Then it starts to challenge that from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל mentioned only the skin, it sounds like the stomach contents, the curdling material, are permitted. The משנה says the stomach of a נבילה is forbidden, which seems to contradict that. Steps 20 and 21 complete the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (introducing an inference)
Itself
But did he really say?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the stomach skin with the stomach contents. שמואל spoke only about the skin, and the challenge is that the משנה forbids the stomach itself.

phrases.english: This implies the stomach itself is permitted,
phrases.notes: "The stomach itself" means what's inside it, the curdling material, as opposed to the skin.

phrases.english: But did שמואל say this?
But didn't we learn:
The stomach of a gentile and that of a נבילה —
phrases.notes: The משנה is in חולין קטז. "Of a gentile" means an animal a gentile slaughtered.

phrases.english: it is forbidden,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קֵיבָה גּוּפָא שַׁרְיָא, וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from שמואל's words in step 18 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of שמואל's words that the stomach contents are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says the stomach of a נבילה is forbidden, which seems to contradict the idea that its contents are permitted.

steps.title: Recalling an old question: isn't a גוי's slaughter already a נבילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion of the משנה about the stomach of a נבילה. There they asked why the משנה lists 'slaughter by a גוי' separately, since an animal slaughtered by a גוי is a נבילה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed that משנה and asked: Is an animal slaughtered by a גוי not a נבילה? Why list it separately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It brings back an old question about the משנה so it can then quote שמואל's answer to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions both 'slaughter by a גוי' and 'נבילה', as if they were two separate things. But according to הלכה, an animal slaughtered by a גוי already has the status of a נבילה. So why mention it twice? This question is the setup that leads to שמואל's own explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (an earlier discussion of a source)
Is that to say...? (introduces a puzzled question)
An animal slaughtered by a non-Jew
An animal that was not properly slaughtered

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה from the last step that forbids the stomach of a נבילה.

phrases.english: Is that to say that an animal slaughtered by a gentile is not a carcass?
phrases.notes: The משנה lists both separately, which is what seems strange.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ, אַטּוּ דְּגוֹי לָאו נְבֵלָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה cited in step 19 by recalling an earlier question about its wording, preparing to quote שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה list 'slaughter by a גוי' separately from נבילה, if they have the same status?

steps.title: שמואל himself said the stomach contents are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answered that the משנה teaches one rule: the stomach of an animal slaughtered by a גוי is a נבילה and forbidden. This shows שמואל holds that the stomach contents of a נבילה are forbidden, which contradicts what his cheese reason implied.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The משנה is teaching one single thing. The stomach of an animal slaughtered by a גוי is a נבילה, and it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמואל's own answer to the old question. That answer sharpens the challenge against him: he himself treats the stomach contents of a נבילה as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 שמואל blamed only the stomach skin, which hinted that the contents are permitted. But here שמואל reads the משנה as saying that the stomach contents of a גוי's slaughter count as נבילה and are forbidden. So שמואל seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches one single thing (not two separate cases)
Stomach, here meaning the curdled milk inside the stomach
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question from the beginning. It is the end of the challenge from step 19: שמואל's own words in another place seem to clash with his reason for forbidding cheese.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: It is teaching one thing:
The stomach of an animal slaughtered by a gentile is a carcass, and it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: Read 'נבלה' as explaining the first part: the גוי's slaughter counts as a נבילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's answer to the question in step 20, which completes the challenge against his view from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reason for forbidding cheese (step 18), which implies the stomach contents of a נבילה are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself explains the משנה to mean that the stomach of a גוי's slaughter is forbidden as נבילה. So he holds the contents are forbidden, which contradicts the implication of his cheese reason.

steps.title: The גמרא says the contradiction is not difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces 'לא קשיא', meaning there is no real contradiction in שמואל's words. The explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer. It declares that שמואל does not really contradict himself, and the explanation will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' tells us the גמרא will resolve the clash between step 18 and step 21. The explanation itself comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved

phrases.english: It is not difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the contradiction raised in steps 19 to 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Announcement that the contradiction will be resolved; the explanation itself comes on the next amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seems to contradict himself about whether the stomach contents of a נבילה are forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: On this amud the גמרא only states that there is no real contradiction in שמואל's words. The explanation comes on the next amud.
